- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion zones; if 3–5 consecutive days show price below 10-day moving average, increase forecast by 1–2% to align with reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for final 7–10 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model often misjudges momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
